What Game has the best Replay-ability?

Probably quite the generic answer i'm about to give, but I'd say skyrim, i'm 55 hours in and I could restart right now and still find new things to do.

My second choice would be Civ 5 (with all the dlc).

My answer has the same pattern. Fallout 3 & NV, I've played over 800hrs of those two put together. I play an original run, then wait 2yrs for all the mods & DLC, mod the game to my liking randomize my starting point and rediscover everything because it's now over twice as big as before. In total I think I played them for 4 times each.

I'm also going for Sid Meier's Pirates! on PSP. Games are short, usually less than 5hrs to complete. Because there's many variables that can change and you can approach the game different ways (armada, single strong ship, trading, robbing, politics) and easter eggs do not pop up in every timeline it's always great fun.

Honorable mentions to chess, pokemon and DOW Soulstorm Apocalypse Multiplayer

I wouldn't say Skyrim has much replayability. It's very shallow, the character creation doesn't do much (other than cosmetically) and any character you roll can end up being identical and doing identical things to any other character, especially since all the quest lines are linear. It has a lot of content, but the content doesn't vary which, for me, is a major factor in replayability.

Playing the game as just a random citizen of skyrim makes the game loads more fun, especially when you add some mods to it, the game can be played for years to come, it all about how invested you are in immersing yourself with the character you play being you.

Especially skyrim with mods, that's unbelievable how much a community can change a game, but stuff like frost fall, or requiem, adding proper lighting, it makes it brand new, I have more than 200 hours in skyrim. And if it wasn't for elite dangerous, which I can never finish, I'd probably still be playing it non stop

I'd agree, though I'd rope in all 3 of the modern Elder Scrolls games. And Oblivion and Skyrim with mods that give you better character customization (like Requiem, SkyRe, or PerkMa). Though even in vanilla Skyrim I always set out a character path and stick to it rather than the jack of all trades max all skills route (like everyone does on their first playthrough!). Get immersed in the character and roleplay to an extent and the game can be played over and over again so many times and so many different ways.

Those games and Civ V are my go to replayable games, so yeah, in total agreement here.
GTA 4. I put over 500 hours on the PC version. GTAV is already at 150ish. Any open world games get me.

Super Smash Brothers. Personally I like Wii U version. There are so many characters to learn, there are so many items and stages to learn, and there are so many customizations all of these that you could play this game forever.

Yes, I know you can say that about almost all multiplayer centric games, but I find that this game just doesn't get old. It has an amazing staying power.

Assumptions - Replayability is a combination of joy, total amount of content, and non-linear gameplay

  1. Civ 4 - have played over 400 hours, mostly with a friend hotseating. We got to the point in one game where multiple handwritten treatise were created.
  2. Oblivion - my favorite place to get lost.
  3. Path of Exile - Always have three hardcore characters going. It makes farewells easier. While the story is super arpg linear, character progression is a tinkerer's paradise.

Honorable Mention - Any spiritual or actual sucessors and predecessors to the top 3.

I stopped the list here before I got greedy.
Minecraft. It's completly up to you what you do in each particular world. Playing since beta and haven't really been bored so far. And the sky is actually the limit. :)

Dawn of War Dark Crusade base game gets you an easy 200. Firestorm Over Kronus can easily double the gameplay value. Castlevania Circle of the Moon, unlocking thief, wizard and the other modes gives you a lot more things to do and more opportunities to discover new rooms and item drops. Age of Empires II and New Vegas are also up there.
Street Fighter 4. Literally it lasted thousands of hours and nearly a decade and people are still finding new ways to play.
Rogue-likes such as Isaac, FTL, and Risk of Rain get a ton of replays from me.

It's really dependent on what people like. There are of course lowest common denominator games that nearly anyone can get hours of moderate enjoyment out of. Skyrim, Tetris, WoW, but past the couple hundred hour mark you get into a more intimate experience detailed especially to your interests.

So if you look at it by that criteria, what game have I replayed the most and put the most hours in to, it would likely mean Chrono Cross for the original Playstation. Between the three physical copies and then various iterations of emulation I have probably completed it a hundred times or more, because it hooks me in all the right ways. The story was great, the game evolves and differs on further playthroughs so that if you play through for a third time on your original save file there are differences from the story and events on the first two times, and there are over forty characters you can unlock to help you along the way.

The music is fantastic, and to this day suits what is going on better than any other game soundtrack I have ever experienced. The combat system relies on slotting abilities you have to spend in combat, and each use of an ability effects your enemies resistance and how they respond, which makes it very deep in the way you can build to overcome encounters but just random enough to keep it from getting boring where you can just overlevel and hammer a single attack button while watching youtube or tv the way I wind up doing with most every other rpg or tactics game.

In short, it personally suited my specific criteria in terms of setting, character variety, unique combat I have to pay attention to, engaging story and sheer amount of things to discover and details to notice. The next closest for me is Radiata Stories also by Square -Enix, which ticks all of the same boxes on my mental playlist. Everyone has their own tastes, but theses two are my favorites. Your personal mileage may vary.
Sonic the Hedgehog 2 is 20+ years old and I still play it. It's just the perfect platformer.
I've always been more of a fan of 3 and knuckles, 2 was the first sonic game I ever played though.
Perfect I dunno if I can agree with that, but it is a damn good game. Super Mario Brothers 3 will always be the perfect platformer for me followed by the warp tunnel levels in Super Mario Sunshine.
I'd suggest maybe Saints Row 3 and 4, I replay it quite often. I also like to replay GameDev Tycoon because of obvious reasons.
For me personally, Dragon Age Origins. I think its more nostalgia than anything else. Modding it helps too!
2008 veteran. Get on my level..
5 years later and I'm still playing TF2. Never bought anything but a single key to "unlock" the full backpack.
Nethack, or something similar. Procedurally generated dungeon crawling with perma-death. The game is two decades old now and people are still playing it and still haven't found the fucking amulet...

Sims, RTS and TBS naturally favour replay-ability, as well as other non-linear games like sandbox games or open world RPG's. That's what makes a lot of those games great. It's a lot harder to achieve it in more linear games though, so I think it's impressive in particular when linear games make you want to keep playing them. Games like Resi4 deserve a huge amount of credit, and the MGS series too. I probably played through MGS3 about 8 or 9 times.
I always find myself going back to oblivion after all these years.

Elite dangerous for me, the game is perfect for unwinding for a bit, which honestly makes you feel good from the money you make, or the distance you've travelled, the game s really rewarding, and you always just pick up where you left off, some people find it boring, but in my opinion it's all about how immersed in the game you are, if your Jacob that plays a game you might not want to play it as much as I do, but if you say you're Jacob, the bounty hunting, guitar salesman, that's been on the search for the next habitibal world to call home, you'll fall in love with it.

The rails hiss as a train roars over the tracks off in the distance, I'm back in my home town or rather on my way out of it. Tucson, Az weather forecasts 90+ degrees for the next week. All I can think of as my heart races is getting out, I've got every thing I need, a few bottles of water, a hooded jacket and my dog Eros. I've been trying to get out for the past couple of days, the problem being is I'm in the wrong spot and I know it. Hoping that by some chance an west bound train may stop at the east bound hop out. No such luck. Hopping out as it's called is a pretty straight forward concept, some times an arduous task in practice some times it can be no hassle at all. For me hopping out in a yard is a romantic affair. I court the train yard by walking the tracks on both sides, trying to get a good feel for how things are operating. Sure it's alot harder than some other options but I prefer it.

It garnishes some kind of security, although I have had few run in's and close call's I've strained to out live my life style. In the quite moment's just before I go to sleep I think about the past. Not any particular event or occurrence I just mull through the memories.

I think back to Austin, Tx I remember all the good time's I managed to had despite loosing my dog Mika. I abstained as I have always done when I loose some thing priceless. I think about all the good times we had together. I think about how that night I gave he an incredibly curt goodbye with a brash pat on the head. Then I think back to the time when I first went to Oceanside, Ca. How she stole my cinnamon roll and that lady took me to her Church and Lunch. How when We left Her in the Yard that She Assured me was dog proof. Not five minutes after we sat down in the front pew's that the back pews went up in childish laughter as my dog trotted along greeting all the children along her way to me. That was 5 years ago next month.

I've tried to live the normal "life" before, numerous times, last year was an astounding learning experience for me. I learned a few things about working in bars, fine dining and slum sandwhich shops along the way. Working for 5 months, trying to juggle a dog that I refuse to abandon, living out side and finally scrounging enough money to rent a room. All seemingly for nothing as I lost it all. It's a gamble the life I live will it devour me into a void nothingness or will I triumph my self and my circumstances to stand tall as a beacon of hope for people struggling to pursue happiness such as I do every day.

Back to the present the aimless what could haves are gone and the train is clicking. I've been walking the fence line for about 30 minutes now and the train that pulled up is fix'n to go west. I throw my backpack first then Eros over the fence. bounding over the fence. I've got one train to go past to get to mine I crawl under and right in front of me is a 48' in a 53' otherwise known as a "bucket".

I've made it onto the train, for me this is the most stressful time spent on a train, waiting for it to move. Will some one see me? Would they care? A rapid series of "Click" "Click" "Click" is a sure sign my ride is about to go.

The first thing I do as I pull out of my old dusty home town is smoke a victory joint and give Eros a nice treat as the sun rises innocently over Tucson. No hints that it will be scorching hot within hours and I will be at the beach basking in the salty cool air of the ocean.

The few bottles of water that I thought would be enough turned out to run out faster than I expected as we sat for 55 minutes in the Sonoran dessert some where in between Yuma,Az and Los Angeles, CA I ran out of water. How ever I was in luck they always keep a few bottles of water on the engine the next time it stops I'd be risking getting left behind in the middle of no where with no water. As the sun high above roasts me to a nice red finish. There is only one thought going through my mind air conditioning. Worth it.

The subtle signs of stopping are abound, the 160 decibels of a train screeching to a hault. I gather my meager belongings into my pack and get ready to jump. The 1/16th of a mile that I ran to get to that engine was the worst run I've ever had to do. The whole way there Eros refused to run but would rather smell the beautiful and abundant flowers in the endless sea of sand.

It wasn't long till I was in the engine and blasting the A/c and pouring bowl after grateful bowl of water. Little did I know some one saw me boarding the unit. This is where shit hits the fan and hits the fan hard. We grind to a stop right in front of a boarder patrol check point. For what it's worth I tried to hide in the bathroom but that didn't fly.

I hear them boarding "Looks like some one was here." then the go for the bathroom I'm locked in and know I'm fucked so I state my citizen ship and that I will cooperate. I'm faced with two choices Option A. I can stay on the train but as soon as I stop I'll be facing a Rail Detective. Option B. I can start walking.

Obviously I chose the hard route I started walking with no guarantees of any thing happening at all. After all the Boarder patrol said there was a town two miles down the road.

Five miles and 3 hours later I get to this "town" the town of abandoned trailer park, Ca. I was lucky enough to catch two rides to Indio, Ca.
